authors: Alan E. Mather, E. Ulrich Franck
title: Phase Equilibria in the System Carbon Dioxide-Water at Elevated Pressures
experimental_method: Synthetic method in a variable-volume nickel-superalloy autoclave with sapphire window (Lentz apparatus): weighed water and CO2 filled, heated isochorically; the two-phase to one-phase transition (dew point) observed visually on heating and on cooling, in some cases confirmed by a discontinuity in the isochoric P-T trace. Water 0.05 uS/cm, CO2 99.99%.
uncertainties_stated: Composition known to about 1%; T and P uncertainties printed per point in Table I (T 0.8-3.5 C, P 1.3-7 MPa).
quality_remarks: Authors say the data support Todheide and Franck (1963) against Takenouchi and Kennedy (1964); the 311 MPa point for 53.0 mol% may indicate the isopleth should shift some degrees to higher T above 250 MPa. Two pressure uncertainties printed as '+- 7' (114.4 and 264.5 MPa rows) may be misprints for 0.7. Temperature scale not stated.
how_extracted: pdf_text_layer (OCR layer of a scanned page) checked cell by cell against the 250 dpi page image; all cells typed from the image
not_extracted_tables: PDF page 1 upper part: end of a preceding J. Phys. Chem. article (nitrobenzene electron hopping), not this paper. No other tables; Figures 1-4 show literature curves (interpolated) and these data points only.
extraction_notes: The paper starts at the lower half of journal p. 6 after the end of another article; Table I on p. 7 belongs to Mather and Franck. The printed +- values were split into separate CSV columns. Mixture mole fraction printed only on the first row of each group (fill_down in mapping). Sanity: rows within each mixture are not ordered by T or P (printed order kept); for 0.625 the dew-point temperature is nearly constant (258.5-261.8 C) over 155.8-264.5 MPa, for 0.530 T rises from 263.5 to 273.3 C with a non-monotonic sequence; all within the stated 225-275 C and 114-311 MPa.
